text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.7% today to $427.34, continuing a sharp two-week slide of over 10%. The stock sank despite oil prices sitting near $103 per barrel domestically, suggesting the decline isn't driven by crude weakness. Instead, the immediate trigger appears to be today's earnings announcement and quarterly report — both filed this morning — combined with news of a leadership change, either of which could have disappointed investors on forward guidance or strategic direction.

The broader picture adds weight to this: refinery utilization stands at 92.8%, and the company operates in an environment where Big Oil earnings are expected to surge, yet analysts have been cautioning that guidance matters more than the headline numbers themselves. The stock's 10% two-week drop and today's further decline suggest the market is pricing in either softer-than-expected guidance from Marathon or concern about how leadership transitions could affect strategy going forward.
